hints: Notice the wording: total input is $E$ and wasted energy is $Q$, so first write the remaining useful energy in terms of $E$ and $Q$.
Recall efficiency is defined as $\text{useful output} / \text{total input}$ for energy or power.
Divide your expression for useful energy $E - Q$ by $E$ and simplify to the form $1 - Q/E$.
walkthrough: Identify the given energies: total supplied energy is $E$ and wasted energy is $Q$.
State the rule: $\text{efficiency} = \text{useful energy output} / \text{total energy input}$.
Find useful energy by conservation: $\text{useful} = E - Q$ because the rest after wasting $Q$ does useful work.
Split the fraction: $(E - Q)/E = E/E - Q/E = 1 - (Q/E)$.

options.A: This is $Q/E$, the fraction of $E$ that is wasted, not the fraction that does useful work.
options.B: This gives a negative value since $Q/E < 1$, whereas efficiency must be between 0 and 1.
options.C: Useful energy is $E - Q$, so efficiency is $(E-Q)/E = 1 - Q/E$.
options.D: This subtracts energy $Q$ from the pure number 1, which is not homogeneous and cannot give efficiency.
